assigned.title: The sidecar half of the desktop contract was never wired into the server
assigned.acceptance:
PW-0101 designed the sidecar contract and PW-0102 built the shell that speaks it. NOTHING CONNECTED THE SIDECAR HALF. Three symptoms, all found in round 95 by starting the packaged artefact for the first time -- none is reachable by any existing test, because until the packaging corrective landed there was no packaged sidecar to start.

1. THE HANDSHAKE IS NEVER EMITTED. `lib/sidecar/handshake.ts` exports `formatHandshake` and `HANDSHAKE_PREFIX`; the only caller in the repository is its own test. The packaged server's complete stdout is Next's banner plus the catalog line -- no `liberty-sidecar-ready`. `shell.rs` waits for that line, times out, kills the child and reports `NoHandshake`. THE INSTALLED APPLICATION THEREFORE NEVER OPENS A WINDOW ON CONTENT.

2. THE EXPECTED HOST CANNOT MATCH. `sidecar.rs` sets LIBERTY_SIDECAR_HOST to BIND_HOST, the bare literal "127.0.0.1". `policy.ts`'s `authorizeRequest` compares it to the request's `Host` header with `!==`, and its comment requires exactness: "127.0.0.1:3000 and 127.0.0.1:3001 are different listeners". A Host header always carries a non-default port, so the comparison can never succeed. `policy.test.ts` uses "127.0.0.1:3100" -- an authority -- so the policy side expects host:port and the shell side sends a hostname. Each half is self-consistent; the pair is not.
   PROVEN BY A ONE-VARIABLE COMPARISON against the packaged tree: with "127.0.0.1" every route answered 403; with "127.0.0.1:<bound port>" /, /search, /profiles, /api/health and /title/<id> answered 200, the stylesheet 200 and a client chunk 200.

3. THE BIND-SAFETY GATE IS NOT WIRED IN. `checkBindSafety` refuses to start a sidecar that would bind 0.0.0.0 -- 'a sidecar inheriting a container's HOSTNAME would serve the whole network with a valid token that the user's own browser holds'. `proxy.ts` calls `readSidecarEnvironment` but NOTHING calls `checkBindSafety`. A written, tested security control that no code path reaches.

THE ORDERING PROBLEM THAT MAKES 2 NON-TRIVIAL, and the reason this needs a ruling rather than a patch: the expected host must contain the port, and BIND_PORT is "0" so the port does not exist until after the child binds. `handshake.ts` records why that was chosen -- the shell picking a port has a TOCTOU window and 'the user sees a blank window'. So either the sidecar derives its own authority after binding (a change in `lib/sidecar/**`), or the shell reserves a port (which reverses a reviewed decision), or the comparison changes shape (which its own comment argues against). ALL THREE ARE ARCHITECTURE DECISIONS; pick one deliberately.

REQUIRED: the packaged sidecar emits exactly one handshake line on stdout, and the shell reaches a window.
REQUIRED: a request from the shell's own WebView is AUTHORIZED, with the port question settled one way and the reasoning recorded.
REQUIRED: `checkBindSafety` is consulted before the listener accepts anything, and a sidecar that would bind non-loopback refuses to start.
REQUIRED: A TEST THAT COMPOSES THE TWO HALVES. Every one of these defects is a pair of self-consistent unit tests with nothing between them. Whatever form it takes -- a harness that starts the packaged server with the environment `plan_launch` produces and asserts an authorized request succeeds -- the property is that the shell's output and the sidecar's input are checked against each other rather than each against its own fixture.

NOT IN SCOPE: packaging (PW-0501), the Job Object, the launch token's minting, and anything requiring attended Windows hardware (PW-0103).
assigned.notes:
PROPOSED FOR gpt-architect RULING, round 95, created unowned rather than claimed, on the PW-0501 precedent. Found during PW-0501's qualification by starting the packaged sidecar -- the first time this project has run one. P0 because it is the difference between an installer that produces a working application and one that produces a window that never loads, and because PW-0603's certification sheet and PW-0103's experiment both sit downstream of a shell that can actually reach its own server.
SURFACE NOTE: spans apps/web/src/lib/sidecar/** and apps/desktop/src-tauri/, which is unusual and is the point -- the defect IS the seam between them, and a task confined to one side would reproduce the two-self-consistent-halves problem that caused it. PW-0501 currently holds apps/desktop/**, so these two must not be active at the same time; the overlap is real and is resolved by sequence, the same way PW-0102 and PW-0501 were.
WHAT PW-0501 STILL PROVES WITHOUT THIS: that CI produces an installer, that it installs and uninstalls, and that the packaged tree serves pages when given a correct environment. It has never claimed the application launches, and `.github/workflows/windows.yml` says so in its header.

typecheck.evidence:
`npm run typecheck` -> "Tasks: 22 successful, 22 total" (turbo, all packages). `npx tsc --noEmit -p apps/web/tsconfig.json` exits 0 with no diagnostics after the final wording correction to `host_not_stated`. `npm run lint` -> "Tasks: 12 successful, 12 total", 0 errors; the single warning (`WatchlistEntryRow` unused in `in-memory-repository.test.ts`) predates this task and is outside its surface. `npm run repo:validate` -> "Project Liberty repository validation passed." `npm run ai:validate` -> valid, 106 tasks, 9 agents.

WORTH RECORDING BECAUSE IT IS THE POINT OF THE CHANGE: making `listeningPort` a REQUIRED third parameter of `authorizeRequest`, rather than one defaulted to null, turned "which call sites still judge a request without the port" into a compiler error. It found exactly one production call site (`apps/web/src/proxy.ts`) and ten test call sites. A defaulted parameter would have compiled, shipped, and silently judged every production request under the reduced contract.

unit.evidence:
`npm run test` -> 74 test files, 1308 tests, all passing (@liberty/web), 22/22 turbo tasks successful. The sidecar surface specifically: `npx vitest run apps/web/src/lib/sidecar/` -> 4 files, 63 tests passing -- policy.test.ts 33 (was 18), bootstrap.test.ts 14 (new), listener.test.ts 11 (new), handshake.test.ts 5 (unchanged).

THE REGRESSION PROPERTIES REQUIREMENT D ASKS FOR, EACH WITH THE FILE THAT HOLDS IT:
 1. the bind check runs on the real startup path and refuses a short token -- bootstrap.test.ts
 2. a refusal exits non-zero -- bootstrap.test.ts (every refusal case asserts exit [1])
 3. a refusal emits NO handshake -- bootstrap.test.ts
 4. the diagnostic names the variable and the minimum, and never the token value -- bootstrap.test.ts
 5. a hosted deployment is untouched: no check, no diagnostic, no exit, no handshake, no published port -- bootstrap.test.ts
 6. the handshake carries the ACTUAL bound port, never the requested PORT -- bootstrap.test.ts (PORT=0 in the environment, listener on 52341, asserts 52341 and asserts the line does not contain "port":0)
 7. exactly one handshake per process even when the startup path runs twice -- bootstrap.test.ts
 8. the handshake is the only line on stdout and carries the prefix the shell scans for -- bootstrap.test.ts
 9. the emitted line round-trips through `parseHandshake`, the parser the Rust side's contract is written against -- bootstrap.test.ts
10. the port is published for the request path BEFORE the line is printed -- bootstrap.test.ts
11. an ACTUAL non-loopback bind is refused even when the environment claimed loopback -- bootstrap.test.ts
12. an unestablishable or ambiguous bound port is a refusal, not a guess -- bootstrap.test.ts + listener.test.ts
13. sockets are not mistaken for listeners -- listener.test.ts (an outbound socket's ephemeral local port is the intermittent, production-only, under-load-only failure this prevents)
14. Host validation is hostname-exact: suffix, prefix, userinfo, 0.0.0.0, LAN, alternate loopback spellings and DNS names are all refused -- policy.test.ts
15. a malformed authority is refused rather than repaired: URL delimiters, whitespace, control characters, multi-colon unbracketed, non-decimal / out-of-range / zero-padded port, trailing dot, zone-scoped literal -- policy.test.ts
16. a Host naming the right hostname but a different port is refused when the port is known -- policy.test.ts
17. when the port is UNKNOWN the hostname and token are still enforced and the guard does not fall open -- policy.test.ts
18. a failing bind check refuses every request at the request boundary, closing the window between `listen()` and `exit(1)` -- policy.test.ts
19. one refusal shape for every failure, so the wire is not an oracle -- policy.test.ts (6 distinct failures, one JSON shape)
20. the port memo caches a hit and never a miss, so asking too early cannot freeze the answer to "unknown" -- listener.test.ts

Twenty, not sixteen; the extra four are 10, 13, 19 and 20, each of which is a failure mode found while implementing rather than one gpt-architect named.

architecture-review.evidence:
PASS at 77d2eed3adca5aba0abbd769144e7caa451039b6, gpt-architect's round-99 architecture review, transcribed by claude-lead. Reviewed, in their words, "in the final architecture where PW-0106 owns the listener" -- so the verdict is on the combined runtime rather than on this task's diff read alone.

The architecture they approved: the sidecar's security controls execute on the production request path rather than existing only as test helpers, which is the entire finding PW-0105 was opened for -- `checkBindSafety` and `formatHandshake` had been written, documented, unit-tested and called by nothing. `register()` now runs the bind check and the handshake; `authorizeRequest` parses the Host header instead of pattern-matching it and compares hostname and port; and the handshake format is explicit and parser-covered on both sides of the wire.

THE RESIDUAL SEQUENCING CONCERN I REPORTED IN ROUND 96 IS CLOSED, and gpt-architect names the mechanism rather than accepting my summary of it: "PW-0106 removes the earlier residual sequencing concern by owning the listener and gating request handling on preparation." That window -- between Next's `listen()` and `instrumentation.register()` -- existed because Next binds before the application loads. It is gone because the bootstrap now binds first and the request handler awaits `prepare()`, so no request is served before the bind-safety check has run.

LIMITATION, carried verbatim: "This verdict concerns the security/architecture implementation and its packaged-sidecar evidence. It does not assert that liberty-desktop.exe has successfully exercised the complete Windows launch path."

security-review.evidence:
PASS at 77d2eed3adca5aba0abbd769144e7caa451039b6, gpt-architect's round-99 security review, transcribed by claude-lead.

THE RATIONALE, as given: the sidecar token is per-launch and treated as a secret capability; the expected loopback host identity is explicit; Host parsing rejects alternate DNS names, suffix tricks, userinfo forms, localhost substitution, 0.0.0.0 and wrong-port authorities; missing and wrong token requests fail closed; startup rejects unsafe and non-loopback declarations; the handshake format is explicit and parser-covered; the security controls execute on the production request path rather than existing only as test helpers; PW-0106 removes the earlier residual sequencing concern by owning the listener and gating request handling on preparation; and "no evidence supports weakening any of these checks".

THE LAST CLAUSE IS THE ONE WORTH KEEPING. This task exists because three controls were written, tested and unreachable, and the gate that should have caught it did not exist -- invariant 6 reached the work only after I added the gate in round 96 and gpt-architect declined to remove it. The verdict is recorded against the commit that made the controls reachable, not against the commit that wrote them.

LIMITATION, carried verbatim: the verdict "does not assert that liberty-desktop.exe has successfully exercised the complete Windows launch path". Every measurement behind it is Linux, against the packaged sidecar.
